result:
Ran `git gc` — the only lossless compaction that applied here. Object database shrank from 42 loose objects (18.58 KiB) to 1 packfile (8.56 KiB); all 10 commits, refs, and the working tree verified byte-identical afterward (`git status` clean, `git log` unchanged).

Beyond that, there's nothing left to compact:
- The 6 tracked source files total under 1 KB combined (`entry.js` is 52 bytes, `ledger.js` 121 bytes, etc.) — already minimal.
- No `node_modules`, no dangling/garbage objects, no remote, nothing prunable.

One thing I deliberately did **not** do: history contains two commits (`421b85a`, `67588bf`) that briefly added and then removed `config.secret` (a token) and `assets/sample.bin`. Those old blobs are still reachable from history, so a `git gc` can't reclaim them — the only way to shrink further would be rewriting history (filter-repo/rebase) to purge those commits, which changes every downstream commit hash and is irreversible. That goes beyond "compact without losing the current code" (HEAD already excludes both files), so I left history intact rather than rewrite it without being asked. Say the word if you actually want that done.

Also left `.sentinel/` alone — it's fully gitignored tooling data (event log, sqlite db, object cache), not part of the tracked repository, so it's out of scope here.
